This Court calls upon the Deputy Commissioner (Sanitation), CMC to explore the possibility of putting the dustbins as a test case in some places in different wards and to evaluate the sanitation position. Burning polythene releases toxic gases that cause air pollution, respiratory issues and even cancer. Non-biodegradable polythene also pollutes land and water, harms animals, and its microplastics can enter the food chain and human bodies, potentially causing long- term health problems like hormonal disruption and cancer. It was submitted that this issue needs to be addressed on emergency basis during upcoming Baliyatra. For food storage, options like reusable silicone or beewax-lined bags, along with glass containers are preferable. Other alternatives include recycled paper bags and various types of bio-degradable and compostable bags, such as those made from plant-based materials like starch or bamboo. Mr. Shibo Toppo, ADM, Cuttack, who is present through virtual mode, has assured this Court that necessary steps for sensitization and administrative steps to stop the use of polythene in Baliyatra shall be taken and viable alternatives which are Registrar (Judicial) vs State Of Odisha & Others .... This Court expects that during Baliyatra, where there would be huge gathering, awareness programme for preventing polythene use and adopting reusable alternatives can be taken by the District Administration which would be for the betterment of the society. The message should be spread through various methods including social media and people should be educated so that the plastic use in our daily lives can be reduced to a great extent. Mr. Avijit Patnaik, Secretary, High Court of Orissa has filed a memo along with a news item published in the vernacular Odia daily dated 28.10.2025, under the heading of "URBAN HATARE GURUTARA ABYABASTHA, MASAKU DASA LAKHYA; TANKA AADAYA KARI BASI JAUCHI CMC" (Serious Disorder in Urban Market, Monthly collection of Rs.10 lakh; CMC collecting money and sitting idle), wherein it is mentioned that the Urban Hat is facing extreme disorder in terms of cleanliness and management. The CMC is collecting dues from small and large traders inside the Urban Hat. Even bicycles and motorcycles parked on the footpath outside the market are being charged parking fees. However, the CMC authorities have forgotten to provide basic amenities in the Urban Hat. Garbage is not being removed from the market. Unauthorized trucks are parked on the road inside the market for loading and unloading goods. Persons are sitting and selling goods inside the market in vehicles. Parking arrangements with payable fees have been made on the footpath paved with paver blocks outside the market. A fee of Rs.10/- is being collected for parking two-wheelers. There is no drinking water facility. Yet, the CMC is collecting Rs.15,000/- to 20,000/- daily from traders in the market. About Rs.20,000/- is also collected daily for vehicle parking. In this way, the urban market collects more than Rs.10 lakh monthly. However, the basic facilities of the Urban Hat remain neglected. The memo along with the news item is taken on record. Relating to the lack of basic amenities in Urban Hat area, Mr. Debasis Nayak, learned counsel for the CMC assures this Court that the same shall be looked into along with the District Administration to take steps to provide a toilet complex and also make provision of safe drinking water. That it is further humbly submitted that before the construction of the Southern gate the residents of the apartment had a verbal communication with the then Commissioner of CMC where the Commissioner had verbally said that there would be no additional approval required for opening of another gate. That the whole purpose of constructing the Southern gate was to get access to a wider road where in time of emergency, an ambulance or a fire truck can travel easily. That it is humbly submitted that the whole case and grievance of the residents of Ward No.22 is installation of vending zone at the said area rather than opening of gates. That the proposed installation of vending zones are constructed on the footpath/ pedestrian path which itself is illegal and against the notification dated 06.07.2015 issued by the Housing & Urban Development Department. A copy of the Notification dated 06.07.2015 is attached herewith. 7. That it is pertinent to submit that the Clause 7(1)(b) of the said notification clearly states that "the vendor in any way shall not obstruct the free movement of the pedestrian and traffic". In this case, the vending zones are constructed right on the footpath creating great problem to larger general public for their free movement. That it is a fact that there is a school just beside the apartment therefore elderly and children are now forced to walk on the road which could possibly lead to a mishap. 8. That it is humbly submitted that in the same said notification, it has been clearly stated that for the approval of installation of vending zones at different place, a Town Planning Committee has to be formed for the purpose of identifying existing street vendors and for registration, the Town Planning Committee shall use Geographic Information System (CIS) mapping, digitalized photo senses, biometric sensors. That has the Opp. Party followed all these above mentioned rules? 9. That it is humbly submitted that this Hon'ble Court had directed that the Opp. Party may see some suitable alteration of installing vending zones but they have kept quiet on that part. That there are more suitable places like near Meria Bazar route to Baropathar road where vending zones can easily be installed. That it is further humbly submitted that in Ward No.22 there are many vending zones constructed leaving spaces for pedestrian but here they have created on the pedestrian/footpath. That the CMC can easily use the 30 feet footpath created from Baropathar to Meria Bazar which has footpath on both sides of the road for such vending zones without obstructing ingress and egress of the traffic." , Mr. Nayak, learned AGA submits that the instructions of the Chief Engineer-cum-Additional Secretary, H & U.D. Department vide his letter No. 12310 dated 30.05.2025 to the Commissioner, C.M.C. to have the DPR relating to the BSWC drains to be vetted by the IIT, Bhubaneswar is his own opinion since, it is on record that the in the review meeting dated 30.04.2025, the issue was never discussed nor referred to. He further submits that since the Government has decided that WATCO would be given "overall supervision" of the project and IIT Bhubaneswar will be involved in the Technical Committee to be constituted for overall technical supervision during execution of the project, the decision of the Government in this regard conforms to the spirit of the Court's observations.
